docs.title: Where to begin
docs.text:
The PlayStation 4 version of Bloodborne, running natively on Linux and the Steam Deck: the game's own code runs on the CPU and its graphics are translated to Vulkan. You need your own dump of the game with update 1.09; no game files are included.

Getting startedYour dump, the AppImage and the first launch. Playing onlineSeamless Hunt, The Hunter's Dream or your own server, and seamless co-op. Steam and the Steam DeckAdd to Steam, Game Mode, controllers and the Steam overlay. When something breaksCommon problems, and how to send a log.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• Online and co-op: messages, bloodstains, bells and summons, and seamless co-op that lasts through deaths, lamps and areas, with Linux and Windows players together.
  • Local co-op: 2 to 4 players on one PC, each with their own controller.
  • Hunter's Atlas: a fullscreen in-game map with fast travel to the lamps you have found.
  • Frame rate unlocked or capped at 30, 60 or 90, from 720p to 4K, and ultrawide screens.
  • FSR 3.1, FSR 4 and DLSS upscaling.
  • Any controller, with its own button prompts in the game, and keyboard and mouse.
  • Trophies, Discord status and Add to Steam in one click.
  • An AppImage for any distribution and the Steam Deck, which updates itself.

docs.title: Game compatibility
docs.text: bbport runs Bloodborne for PS4 with update 1.09. Its hooks and patches use the addresses of one executable: the launcher hashes the loaded eboot.bin image and runs only that one 1.09 executable (scripts/game_check.py). A dump that passes the check runs; one that does not is told why (no 1.09 update, another executable, or an eboot.bin with Lance McDonald's 60 fps patch baked in).

docs.text:

Edition Region Title ID Content ID 1.09 executable checked Bloodborne US CUSA00900 UP9000-CUSA00900_00-BLOODBORNE000000 Yes Bloodborne Europe CUSA00207 EP9000-CUSA00207_00-BLOODBORNE0000EU Not yet Bloodborne UK CUSA00208 EP9000-CUSA00208_00-BLOODBORNE0000UK Not yet Bloodborne Japan CUSA00299 JP9000-CUSA00299_00-BLOODBORNE0000JP Not yet Bloodborne Asia CUSA01363 HP9000-CUSA01363_00-BLOODBORNE0000AS Not yet The Old Hunters Edition US CUSA03179 UP9000-CUSA03179_00-BLOODBORNE000000 Not yet Game of the Year Edition Europe CUSA03173 EP9000-CUSA03173_00-BLOODBORNE0000EU Yes The Old Hunters Edition Japan CUSA03014 JP9000-CUSA03014_00-BLOODBORNE0000JP Not yet The Old Hunters Edition Asia CUSA03023 HP9000-CUSA03023_00-BLOODBORNE0000AS Not yet

Checked means a dump of that release with update 1.09 had exactly the executable bbport runs. The others are accepted on the expectation that every release shares the same 1.09 executable; if one does not, the launcher says so instead of starting a game that would crash. A report of how yours goes is welcome either way.

The alpha tests (CUSA01318, CUSA01322, CUSA01333, CUSA01335) are not supported.

The Game of the Year and The Old Hunters editions include the DLC. With a base game (such as the US CUSA00900), dump your add-ons too: each one is a folder (SPEXPANSIONDLC03, SPDLCMESSENGER00…) with only sce_sys inside, because their data ships with the 1.09 update. Put them in one folder and choose it in the launcher (Setup → DLC folder), or set BB_DLC_DIR=/path/to/dlc for run.sh; the launcher shows how many it found. Each folder must keep the add-on's name (its entitlement label, such as SPEXPANSIONDLC03). Copying them to user/addcont/<title id>/, shadPS4's layout, works too.

docs.title: Tested with this fork
docs.text:
On Linux (CachyOS, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060), with the US release (CUSA00900):

  • The base game with update 1.09 and the add-ons dumped separately (The Old Hunters and the two messenger add-ons), from the launcher's DLC folder.
  • A dump whose eboot.bin had Lance McDonald's 60 fps patch baked in: the launcher reports it, and the clean 1.09 eboot.bin runs.
  • Both regional texts through Game region: Spanish from Spain (Europe) and Latin American Spanish (the Americas).

The European Game of the Year edition (CUSA03173) is the release the original bbport is developed and tested with.

docs.title: Catching a crash with a debugger
docs.text:
By default a fatal fault or a GPU-library assertion ends the process at once: the log keeps one line (Host fault, Guest fault, STOP: GPU library assertion failed) and nothing else. BB_FAULT_WAIT=1 keeps the process alive at that point, stopped inside its handler, so a debugger can look at the faulting thread with its registers, stack and memory still there.

  1. Launcher → Advanced → Developer → Extra variables: BB_FAULT_WAIT=1 (or export it before run.sh). Nothing changes while the game runs; it costs nothing.
  2. When it crashes, the game freezes, a desktop notification says so, and the log ends with bbport: ... the process stays alive for a debugger: bash tools/debug_attach.sh <pid>.
  3. Run that line. gdb attaches, writes logs/crash-<time>-<pid>.txt and kills the process. With --keep it detaches instead, so gdb -p <pid> can be used by hand afterwards.

The report has every thread's stack, and for the faulting thread its registers, the instructions around pc and the top of its stack; for a GPU-library assertion the locals of the asserting thread (bt full). bbport's own frames carry file and line (the build is RelWithDebInfo); libc's come from debuginfod when it is reachable. Game code shows as a guest offset (pc minus the image base, as in the log's Guest fault line); the report gives an objdump command that disassembles out/boot-linked.bin around it.

GPU hangs are different: the device is lost and the GPU breadcrumbs in the log name the stuck draw or dispatch; the assertion that follows is caught the same way, but the state of interest is on the GPU.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: The port reads a few hundred environment variables. Some are for players (upscaler, frame rate, controls). Most are diagnostics and developer switches. This page lists every variable found in src/, gpu/, bbsc/, scripts/, launcher/, run.sh, packaging/ and tools/, with what the code does with it. The information comes from the code on main (0.51-linux.16). When a comment and the code disagree, the code wins.

docs.title: How to set them
docs.text:
In the launcher: go to Advanced → Developer → Extra variables (NAME=value, space-separated). The settings key is extra_env in the launcher's settings.json. The field is parsed in game_environment() (launcher/bbport_launcher.py:693):

for item in s["extra_env"].split():
    if "=" in item:
        key, value = item.split("=", 1)
        env[key] = value
  • The field is split on whitespace. Each piece is split at its first =: BB_UPSCALER=fsr4 BB_AUDIO_GAIN=1.5 RADV_DEBUG=nohiz.
  • There is no quoting. A value cannot contain spaces, and quotes are kept literally as part of the value (BB_X="a" gives "a" with the quotes). Use separators the variable itself accepts, such as ; or ,.
  • A piece without = is ignored without any message. If a name appears twice, the last one wins.
  • Any name is accepted, including third-party ones (RADV_DEBUG, MANGOHUD, VK_*, __GL_*).
  • The result goes to run.sh. Both the launcher's Play button and --play (Steam shortcut, Steam Deck game mode) use it.

From a terminal (source checkout): BB_GAME_DIR=/path/to/CUSA03173 BB_FPS=60 bash run.sh. Without the launcher, nothing sets the launcher's variables. run.sh then uses its own defaults (game folder ../CUSA03173, uncapped frame rate, and so on).

From a terminal (AppImage): BB_UPSCALER=fsr4 ./Bloodborne-bbport-x86_64.AppImage --play starts the game with the launcher's saved settings. Mind the precedence below: the launcher's own settings replace a variable of the same name from the shell. Extra variables replace both. The AppImage keeps its data (bbport.ini, saves, logs) in BB_DATA_DIR, by default ~/.local/share/bbport.

bbport.ini: many graphics options live in bbport.ini and the in-game menu, not in the environment. A few variables override those keys at start: BB_UPSCALER, BB_UPSCALE_PRESET, BB_FSR_SHARPNESS, BB_JITTER, BB_REACTIVE* and BB_OBJECT_MOTION (gpu/shim/bbport_settings.cpp:192-208). Values set this way stay in force until the next start.

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text:
The environment is built in this order. A later step wins.

  1. The environment the launcher (or the AppImage) was started with.
  2. The launcher's own settings (game_environment(), launcher/bbport_launcher.py:619-698).
  3. Some are always written: BB_GAME_DIR, BB_MODS_*, BB_PROMPTS, BB_GESTURES_NO_MOTION, BB_PATCHES_*, BB_LANGUAGE, BB_REGION, BB_MENU_LANGUAGE, BB_FULLSCREEN, BB_PRESENT_MODE, BB_SKIP_NETWORK_CHOICE, BB_FPS, BB_DISCORD and BB_STEAM_OVERLAY. For these, a shell value is replaced.
  4. Others are written only when the setting is on or not empty: BB_HDR, BB_FPS_LIMIT, BB_DRAW_PIPE, BB_READBACKS, BB_PREUPLOAD, BB_PC_MODEL, BB_GPU_PROFILE, BB_PAD_DEADZONE (only when the dead zone is not 4 %), BB_PAD_LIGHTBAR and others. For these, a shell value survives while the setting is off.
  5. Hunter's Atlas (atlas_environment(), launcher/bbport_launcher.py:598): always BB_ATLAS_ENABLED (0 when the map is off or not prepared); with the map on also BB_MAP_DIR, BB_MAP_ART_DIR, BB_MAP_FONT, BB_MAP_CATALOG, BB_MAP_CONFIG, BB_MAP_TRAVEL_ENABLED, BB_MAP_ITEMS_ENABLED, BB_MAP_ITEM_CATEGORIES, BB_MAP_FOG_ENABLED=0 and BB_MAP_NPC_MODE=all.
  6. Online (only when Play online is on and the online module exists): scripts/online.py environment() adds BB_ONLINE, BB_SHADNET_*, BB_UPNP, BB_COMMUNITY_SERVER, BB_SEAMLESSHUNT_TOMBS, SHADPS4_P2P_* and the BBSC options (scripts/bbsc.py).
  7. Extra variables come last and override everything above, including the launcher's own settings and the BBSC options.
  8. run.sh mostly fills in defaults with ${VAR:-default}, so a value you set is kept. It does force a few:
  9. BB_AS_0_3=1 forces BB_GUEST_IN_PLACE=0, BB_HOST_COPY_WAITS=all and BB_PRODUCER_CHECK=1.
  10. BB_SAVE_LOG=1 forces BB_FRAME_STATS=1.
  11. BB_AUTO_RENDER_RES=1 makes run.sh unset BB_RENDER_RES, BB_OUTPUT_RES and BB_UI_RES, so do not set it by hand.
  12. When bbport.ini asks for a non-1080p output without live resolution and BB_RENDER_RES is unset, run.sh exports BB_RENDER_RES, BB_OUTPUT_RES and BB_DMEM_MB itself.
  13. BB_BBSC_LIB is unset unless BB_BBSC=1 and BB_ONLINE=1.
  14. SHADPS4_HTTP_HOST_OVERRIDES_JSON is rewritten whenever online play is on.
  15. BB_PRESENCE_DIR is rewritten when Discord is on, and BB_TROPHY_DIR when the trophy list is prepared.
  16. MANGOHUD is dropped while Steam's own performance overlay (mangoapp) runs.
  17. run.sh exports defaults that differ from the code's built-in ones: BB_COPY_GPU_BUFFERS=1, BB_GPU_WRITE_TWINS=1, BB_GPU_WRITE_TWINS_MAX=65536, BB_PREUPLOAD=1, BB_UFFD=0, BB_GUEST_IN_PLACE=$BB_PC_MODEL, BB_VBLANK_HZ (from BB_FPS) and BB_PC_MODEL (1 on AMD, 0 elsewhere).
  18. libbbsc sets BBSC_MOD_SEAMLESS=0 and SHADPS4_BBSC_FIVE_HUNTERS=0 itself on a public game server (The Hunter's Dream, nodreamforthehunter.com, shadps4.net or scej-network.jp; Seamless Hunt is not one), whatever was asked (bbsc/emulator/mod/linux/bbsc_mod_linux.cpp:360, the list in bbsc/emulator/mod/bbsc_http.cpp:245).

Value formats vary from one variable to another:

  • The shadPS4-style Flag() (gpu/shim/core/emulator_settings.h:14) takes any value starting with 1, y or t as on.
  • Most port switches look at a leading 1, or treat everything but 0 as on.
  • A few logs and traps turn on when set to any value, 0 included.
  • BBSC switches are off only with 0.

The Values column gives the rule for each variable. Where it says "(default X)", that is the behaviour when the variable is unset. In the tables:

  • Launcher: marks variables the launcher writes from a setting. Use the setting rather than the extra field.
  • Internal: marks variables set by run.sh or the package. Leave them alone.

docs.title: Most useful
docs.text: Variable What it does BB_UPSCALER Upscaler at start: off, fsr3, fsr4, fsr411, taa, dlss (overrides bbport.ini/menu). BB_UPSCALE_PRESET Upscaler preset at start: 0 Native AA, 1 Quality, 2 Balanced, 3 Performance, 4 Ultra Performance. BB_FSR_SHARPNESS Upscaler sharpening strength, 0–2 (default 0.5). BB_RENDER_RES Fixed render resolution WxH patched in at start (presets then need a restart). BB_FPS Frame-rate patch: uncap (default), 60, 90 or 30 (launcher: Frame rate → Mode). BB_FPS_LIMIT FPS cap; 0 or unset = no limit (launcher: FPS limit). BB_PRESENT_MODE Vulkan present mode: Mailbox (default), Fifo (vsync), FifoRelaxed or Immediate. BB_DISPLAY Monitor for the window/fullscreen: number or part of its name. BB_GPU_ID Which GPU to use, by Vulkan device index. BB_PC_MODEL Memory model: 1 = new (default on AMD), 0 = the 0.3 one (default elsewhere). BB_DRAW_PIPE Two-stage GPU pipeline, 20–30 % faster: 1 on, 0 off (default on with 8+ CPU threads). BB_PREUPLOAD Background upload into VRAM: 0 off, 1 rewritten memory only (run.sh default), 2 everything (~3 GB more VRAM). BB_ASYNC_PIPELINES 0 makes the game wait for shader compiles instead of skipping a draw for a frame or two. BB_ANISO Anisotropic filtering ratio (default 16; 0 = the game's own). BB_DLSS 0 turns DLSS support off on NVIDIA. RADV_DEBUG / BB_AUTO_NOHIZ AMD GCN 3–5 on RADV: run.sh sets RADV_DEBUG=nohiz unless BB_AUTO_NOHIZ=0. BB_PAD_DEADZONE / BB_PAD_DEADZONE_OUTER Inner (default 5) and outer (default 127) stick dead zones, of 127 (launcher: Controls → Stick dead zone (%), the inner one). BB_MOUSE_DEADZONE Minimum stick deflection used for mouse look (default 16 of 127). BB_AUDIO_GAIN Master volume multiplier, up to 8 (default 1.0). BB_SAVE_LOG 1 saves the log and per-frame statistics to <data>/logs/ (for bug reports). MANGOHUD 1 shows the MangoHud overlay.

The monitor the window and fullscreen go to (issue #69); bb-gpu-capabilities --displays lists them, and the log says which one was taken. Creates the game window fullscreen when the value starts with 1. gpu/shim/window.cpp:116, launcher/bbport_launcher.py:639 BB_GPU_ID Vulkan device index (-1: automatic ranking) Which GPU the game uses, by its index in the Vulkan device list; out of range asserts. bb-gpu-capabilities follows it too. gpu/shim/core/emulator_settings.h:22, gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_instance.cpp:146, tools/gpu_capabilities.c:257 BB_HDR 1/y/t or unset (off) Launcher: Graphics > Display > Allow HDR (set only when on). Allows an HDR swapchain (the colour-space extension and an HDR surface format) when the display offers it. gpu/shim/core/emulator_settings.h:60, gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_swapchain.cpp:246, launcher/bbport_launcher.py:652 BB_LIVE_RES 0 | 1 (default: bbport.ini live_resolution, else off) For output sizes other than 1080p: 1 = live resolution changes (guest at 1080p, host targets scaled at run time, change without restart; slower), 0 = startup resolution patch. Overrides bbport.ini live_resolution=0/1/auto. Outputs wider than 16:9 always take the startup patch. run.sh:75-122 BB_MENU_LANGUAGE en, ru, es, it, fr, de, pt_BR, zh_CN (first two letters compared; unset: LC_ALL/LC_MESSAGES/LANG/LANGUAGE) Launcher: the launcher's own language. Language of the in-game menu until one is chosen in it (bbport.ini menu_language wins). gpu/shim/bbport_settings.cpp:165, launcher/bbport_launcher.py:638 BB_NVIDIA_EGL 0 = off (default on) Packaged builds with the host NVIDIA driver: sets __EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES to the host's EGL vendor files, NVIDIA first (issue #107); 0 leaves it unchanged. launcher/bbport_vulkan.py:116-124 BB_NVIDIA_LIB_DIR directory (default none) Packaged builds: an extra directory searched for the host NVIDIA Vulkan driver library. launcher/bbport_vulkan.py:74-76 BB_OUTPUT_RES WxH Internal (run.sh exports it from bbport.ini output_res for non-1080p outputs without live resolution; unset again on restart). Output size the upscaler fills when the scene is rendered at a startup-patched size (BB_RENDER_RES); also passed to scripts/patches.py. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_temporal_upscaler.cpp:199, run.sh:119, run.sh:190 BB_PRESENT_MODE Mailbox, Fifo, FifoRelaxed, Immediate (Mailbox) Launcher: Graphics > Display > Present mode. Vulkan present mode; a mode the driver lacks falls back to Fifo. Any other value logs an error and uses Mailbox. gpu/shim/core/emulator_settings.h:25, gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_swapchain.cpp:281, launcher/bbport_launcher.py:640 BB_PRESENT_THREAD 0 = off; else on (on) Swapchain work runs on a separate swap thread next to the present thread; 0 runs it on the present thread. gpu/shadps4/core/libraries/videoout/driver.cpp:76-81 BB_RENDER_RES WxH (unset = live resolution path; scene at the menu's preset) Explicitly sets the game's render resolution with a patch at start (the older path). Fixes the scene size: presets and resolution then need a restart, and TAA at another size is refused. docs.text: Variable Values (default) What it does Where BB_ANISO integer (16); 0 = the game's own samplers Mipmapped linear samplers of graphics draws get this anisotropic filtering ratio instead of the PS4's (sharper floors, stairs and walls at grazing angles). gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:3584 BB_AUTO_NOHIZ 0 = off (default 1) On GCN 3–5 GPUs under RADV (Polaris, Vega and their APUs) run.sh sets RADV_DEBUG=nohiz to avoid black halos/missing geometry from depth compression; 0 disables that. Ignored if you set RADV_DEBUG yourself. run.sh:212 BB_DLSS 0 = off; unset = on when available NVIDIA DLSS through the optional bridge library (libbbport_dlss.so + NVIDIA's libnvidia-ngx-dlss). 0 disables it; without the libraries or on other GPUs nothing changes. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_dlss.cpp:176, gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_dlss.h:8 BB_FSR1 1/y/t or 0 (off) shadPS4's FSR 1 pass in the presenter (spatial upscale of the final image); separate from the port's upscalers (bbport.ini upscaler). gpu/shim/core/emulator_settings.h:59, gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_presenter.cpp:175 BB_FSR411_DIR directory (unset = fsr4_411 next to run.sh) Internal (run.sh sets it to /fsr4_411 when that exists). Note: run.sh's startup render size still comes from bbport.ini; only patches.py --print-preset-size honours it. gpu/shim/bbport_settings.cpp:202, scripts/patches.py:513 RADV_DEBUG RADV flags (run.sh may set nohiz) Mesa RADV debug flags; if you set it, run.sh's automatic nohiz for GCN 3–5 (BB_AUTO_NOHIZ) is skipped. run.sh:212

docs.text:
Variable Values (default) What it does Where BB_ASYNC_PIPELINES 0 = off; anything else / unset = on New graphics pipelines of passes drawn every frame compile on worker threads while their draws are skipped for a frame or two, instead of the game standing still for the driver. 0: compiled on the GPU thread, the game waits. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:734, gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_pipeline_cache.h:212 BB_ASYNC_PIPELINE_THREADS integer ≥1 (unset = CPU threads / 4, clamped 1–4) Number of worker threads for BB_ASYNC_PIPELINES. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_pipeline_cache.cpp:643 BB_ASYNC_SUBMIT 0 = off; unset/other = on Submissions go out from the recording threads once their segments are recorded, instead of the GPU thread waiting for them (~65 µs each). Only with recording worker threads. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_scheduler.cpp:150 BB_CONSTANTS_IN_PLACE 1 = on (off) With BB_GUEST_IN_PLACE: small read-only buffers (constants) are read by the GPU where the game wrote them instead of being copied when the draw is decoded or recorded. Experiment toggle bit 1 inverts it at run time. gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:507, gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer.h:57 BB_CONSTRAM_PIPE 0 = off; unset/other = on With the two-stage draw pipe: before the command processor writes guest memory with the CPU (constant RAM dump), it waits only for the queued packets that read those bytes, not all of them. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:900, gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.h:114 BB_COPY_GPU_BUFFERS first char 1/y/t = on; run.sh exports 1 when unset (code default without run.sh: off) Internal. The command buffers of each submission are copied when the game submits them and decoded from the copy (the game reused that memory before the GPU thread got to it: "Unimplemented PM4 type 0" after loading a save). 0 decodes guest memory directly. run.sh:276, gpu/shim/core/emulator_settings.h:56, gpu/shadps4/video_core/amdgpu/liverpool.h:252 BB_COPY_MERGE_KB integer KiB (64) Maximum gap between buffer copies of the game's copy shader (HLE path) that are merged into one batch. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_shader_hle.cpp:203 BB_COPY_SHADER_NATIVE 0 = HLE; unset/other = native With the game's memory in place, the game's buffer copy shader runs as itself (translated). 0: the copy list is read on the CPU and copied by the port (older HLE path). Experiment bit 2 inverts it at run time. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_shader_hle.cpp:272 BB_COPY_THREADS 0-16 (a quarter of the available hardware threads, 1-4) Number of threads that split large guest memory copies. gpu/shim/bbport_copy.cpp:30, src/runtime_memory.c:738 BB_DIRECT_SEGMENT 0 = off; unset/other = on With BB_ASYNC_SUBMIT, commands recorded on the GPU thread (e.g. upscaler passes) get their own command-buffer segment instead of waiting for the recording threads (~90 µs). 0: the wait. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_scheduler.cpp:647 BB_DMEM_MB MiB, 5056–16384 (default 5056; run.sh sets 9152 for render sizes above 1080p) Direct memory size reported to the game (retail PS4: 5056 MiB); the resolution patches above 1080p need more or the game exits at start. src/runtime_memory.c:22-30, run.sh:132, run.sh:132 BB_DRAW_PIPE 1 = on, 0 = off (unset = on with 8+ CPU threads) Launcher: Advanced > Performance > "Two-stage GPU pipeline" (Auto/On/Off). Two-stage GPU command pipeline (decode and record on separate threads): 20–30% faster; turn off if unstable. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:830, launcher/bbport_launcher.py:657 BB_FAULT_SKIP_TEXTURES 0 = off; unset/other = on A write fault on a page no tracked image protects skips the texture cache lock (guest threads no longer wait 0.3–0.6 s behind texture uploads). 0: every fault takes the lock, as before. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:4328 BB_FAULT_WINDOW KiB, clamped 4-1024 and rounded up to a power of two (256) Size of the window unprotected around a guest write fault (write tracking), so neighbouring writes do not fault again. Window at or below one tracker page = feature off. gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:691-698 BB_FPS_LIMIT frames per second; 0 or unset = no limit Launcher: Graphics > Frame rate > FPS limit (set only when > 0). Frames per second the present thread lets through. gpu/shim/core/emulator_settings.h:51, launcher/bbport_launcher.py:655 BB_FRAMES_AHEAD integer ≥0 (1); 0 = no bound The GPU command thread runs at most this many guest frames ahead of the GPU, so GPU-bound frames finish at an even rate instead of in bursts. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_presenter.cpp:475 BB_GARLIC_VRAM 0 = off; any other value on (unset = on, except on integrated GPUs) With the PC memory model, Garlic memory (what the GPU reads a lot: geometry, textures) gets a VRAM copy kept current like a default heap; 0 keeps it in place too. Ignored when the fixed arena is in use. gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:474-479, 2189-2192 BB_GC_IDLE_SECONDS seconds, clamped 1-63 (20) Texture collector: below the pressure mark an image is evicted once unused for this long (the textures of an area left behind). gpu/shadps4/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.cpp:1345, 1367-1371 BB_GC_PRESSURE_IDLE_SECONDS seconds, clamped 0-63 (5) Texture collector: under VRAM pressure an image is evicted once unused for this long (over the critical mark for 1 s first, then by submissions). gpu/shadps4/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.cpp:1379-1388 BB_GC_PRESSURE_PERCENT percent, clamped 10-75 (60) Texture collector, dedicated GPUs below 8 GB: the pressure mark is at least this share of the budget (was 40 %, about what the game holds outside textures, so such cards were under pressure all session). The critical mark is unchanged. gpu/shadps4/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.cpp:62-76 BB_GC_KEEP_GPU_WRITTEN 0 = off; else on (on) Texture collector: images the GPU wrote stay in VRAM until past the critical mark and unused for a minute, linear ones like tiled ones (issue #30). 0: linear ones are downloaded and freed under mere pressure, as before. gpu/shadps4/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.cpp:1453 BB_GC_TILE_BACK 0 = off; else on (on) Texture collector: past the critical mark, a GPU-written tiled image unused for a minute is tiled back into the game's memory before it is freed (issues #13, #14). 0 = dropped unwritten as before, which left the Hunter's Dream black. Multisampled images are always dropped. gpu/shadps4/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.cpp:1435-1470, 201-250 BB_GPU_COMMAND_WRITES 0 = off; unset/other = on With BB_GUEST_IN_PLACE: the game's WRITE_DATA commands are performed by the GPU in stream order, as the PS4 command processor does, instead of a CPU store at decode time. 0: CPU store. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:212, gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.h:204 BB_GPU_LABELS 0 = off; 1 = on; unset = on except on AMD GFX8 (Polaris, RX 4xx/5xx) With BB_GUEST_IN_PLACE and honest labels: end-of-pipe labels (fences) are written by the GPU itself into the game's memory. 0: by a CPU thread after the GPU. GFX8 stalled with GPU-written labels (upstream #203), so it gets the CPU's unless 1. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:301-316 BB_GPU_SPIN_US microseconds, negative = 0 (200 with 12+ hardware threads, else 0) The GPU command thread spins this long before sleeping when it runs out of work, so the next of the ~20 submissions of a frame is picked up without a condition-variable wake-up. 0 = no spinning (saves CPU on small machines). gpu/shadps4/video_core/amdgpu/liverpool.cpp:163-171 BB_GPU_TIMESTAMPS 0 = off; unset/other = on With BB_GUEST_IN_PLACE: the game's GPU timestamps (100 MHz clock) are written by the GPU in stream order. 0: written by the CPU. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:290 BB_GPU_WRITE_TWINS 1 = on; run.sh exports 1 when unset (code default without run.sh: off) Internal. A guest write into a page holding bytes the GPU is still writing (counters, small compute outputs) does not wait for the GPU: the guest's bytes are kept as a "twin". Not with BB_READBACKS=2. run.sh:279, gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:291-306 BB_GPU_WRITE_TWINS_MAX bytes per page; run.sh exports 65536 when unset (code default without run.sh: 1024) Internal. Only pages with at most this many GPU-written bytes get twins; larger outputs (vertices the CPU reads back, FaceGen) keep waiting for the GPU. run.sh:279, gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:296, 308-313 BB_GUEST_GPU_MEMORY 1 = on (off; implied by BB_GUEST_IN_PLACE=1 on a capable GPU) Guest direct memory comes from GPU-visible Vulkan chunks (dma-buf, or host import on NVIDIA) instead of the memfd, so the GPU reads the game's data in place. Disables BB_UFFD (dma-buf cannot be write-protected by userfaultfd). gpu/shim/bbport_guest_memory.cpp:700-718, gpu/shadps4/video_core/page_manager.cpp:723-728, run.sh:195 BB_GUEST_IN_PLACE 1 = on, anything else = off Internal (run.sh: = BB_PC_MODEL, forced 0 by BB_AS_0_3=1; set by hand overrides the memory model). The GPU uses the game's direct memory where it is (GPU-visible chunks) instead of copies in VRAM, and command-processor writes/labels/timestamps are done by the GPU in order. Part of the new memory model (BB_PC_MODEL=1). gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:515, gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer.h:38, run.sh:239 BB_GUEST_MEMORY dmabuf, host, or unset (AMD: dma-buf chunks; other GPUs: host memory import first) How the game's direct memory is made GPU-visible in the new memory model: dma-buf chunks or imported host memory (VK_EXT_external_memory_host). host fails instead of falling back when import does not work. gpu/shim/bbport_guest_memory.cpp:668 BB_GUEST_VRAM 1 or unset (off) Experiment: the game's direct memory in VRAM the CPU maps through the PCI BAR (Resizable BAR), as GDDR is the PS4's one memory: no VRAM copies. gpu/shim/bbport_guest_memory.cpp:37 BB_HONEST_FLUSH_US integer µs (2000; a header comment says 1000) With honest labels: at the end of a guest submission, recorded work that signals wait for is submitted at most once per this interval while the GPU still has work. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:400 BB_HONEST_IDLE_BACKLOG integer bytes (65536) With honest labels: work is not submitted early "because the GPU is idle" while this many bytes of draws are still queued for the recording thread. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:416 BB_HONEST_IDLE_FLUSH 0 = off; unset/other = on With honest labels: signalled work is submitted at once when the GPU has finished everything submitted (instead of waiting for BB_HONEST_FLUSH_US). gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:412 BB_HONEST_LABELS 1 = on (unset = on only with BB_GUEST_IN_PLACE) Fences/labels (EOP, EOS, mem semaphores) are written once the GPU has finished the work before them, as the hardware does, instead of when that work is recorded. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:98, gpu/shadps4/video_core/amdgpu/liverpool.cpp:448 BB_HOST_COPY_WAITS all (unset = only when needed) Internal (run.sh sets all with BB_AS_0_3=1). all: before every guest write, wait for all host copies (the old 0.3 behaviour). Default: wait only when a host copy may still read the written range. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.h:130, run.sh:239 BB_INDIRECT_GUARD 0 = off; unset/other = on Guards indirect compute dispatches: implausible group counts (garbage from particle simulations that caused device lost) are zeroed and the dispatch skipped, and counted in the log. 0: the game's counts as they are. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_indirect_guard.cpp:57, gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_indirect_guard.h:11 BB_INDIRECT_DRAW_GUARD 0 = off; unset/other = on Guards indirect draws: a vertex (or index) count times the instance count past BB_INDIRECT_DRAW_GUARD_MAX (garbage that would keep the GPU busy past the driver's timeout, issue #19) is zeroed and the draw skipped, and counted in the log. An open render pass is paused for the check and continued. 0: the game's arguments as they are. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_indirect_draw_guard.cpp:60, gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_indirect_draw_guard.h:13 BB_INDIRECT_DRAW_GUARD_MAX integer 1–4294967295, decimal or 0x hex (16777216); invalid keeps the default Most vertices (or indices) times instances one indirect draw may run before BB_INDIRECT_DRAW_GUARD skips it. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_indirect_draw_guard.cpp:42 BB_INDIRECT_GUARD_MAX integer 1–4294967295, decimal or 0x hex (4194304); invalid keeps the default Most workgroups one indirect dispatch may launch before BB_INDIRECT_GUARD skips it. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_indirect_guard.cpp:35 BB_LAYER_MEMORY 1 = on, 0 = off (unset = chosen by the memory model per GPU) The layer's memory module: the game's memory bound in place with VRAM copies, without sparse binding (NVIDIA's sparse binding stalls the GPU for seconds). 0: AMD's sparse arena. See BB_PC_MODEL. gpu/shim/bbport_guest_memory.cpp:546, run.sh:204 BB_LAYER_MIRROR_FLOOR_PERCENT percent, max 90 (25) Layer memory module: share of the driver's VRAM budget the VRAM mirrors keep against the texture collector; above it they yield to images, below it images yield. gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:3930 BB_LAYER_MIRROR_GROWTH_MB MiB; 0 = none (64) Layer memory module: the most room a growing VRAM mirror gets above its current end. gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache_layer.cpp:610-616 BB_LAYER_RELOAD_RESET 0 = off; else on (on) Layer memory module: a block the GPU once wrote in place that the loaders then write whole may have a VRAM copy again (dynamic blocks piled up over area loads and lamp travel, lowering the frame rate). 0: kept in place for good, as before. gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:2596 BB_LAYER_UNMAP_RESET 0 = off; else on (on) Layer memory module: blocks the game unmaps whole lose what kept them in place (CPU writes, GPU writes in place, failed watches); memory mapped there again starts as new. 0: as before. gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:3308 BB_LAYER_READ_TRAPS 1 = on (off) What the GPU writes into a VRAM copy only is made no-access for the CPU until it is copied back, so the CPU never reads stale data. Off by default for now. gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache_layer.cpp:1285 BB_LAYER_WATCH 0 = off; else on (on; needs BB_LAYER_WRITE_TRAPS) Layer memory module: blocks the CPU writes unannounced get VRAM copies too, write-trapped and uploaded again after the CPU's next write. gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache_layer.cpp:410-424 BB_PC_MODEL 1 = new | 0 = 0.3 model (default: 1 on AMD GPUs, 0 elsewhere) Launcher: Advanced → "Memory and translation model" (Auto leaves it to run.sh). Memory model: 1 = the GPU uses the game's memory in place and the command processor's work is translated (implies BB_GUEST_IN_PLACE=1); 0 = 0.3 model (VRAM copies, write tracking). A value in extra variables wins over "Auto". run.sh:212, run.sh:199, launcher/bbport_launcher.py:671 BB_PC_MODEL_ANY_GPU 1 or unset (off) Lets the new memory model's sparse arena run on non-AMD GPUs that would otherwise fall back to the 0.3 model (NVIDIA: rebinding memory held the GPU for seconds). gpu/shim/bbport_guest_memory.cpp:513, gpu/shim/bbport_guest_memory.h:35 BB_PIPELINE_CACHE 1/y/t or 0 (1) The port's pipeline cache: shaders are compiled again at startup from the stored list (warm-up). 0 turns it off. gpu/shim/core/emulator_settings.h:64, gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_pipeline_serialization.cpp:330 BB_PIPE_SIGNALS 0 = off; unset/other = on (with honest labels and the draw pipe) Fences, GPU-idle/frame signals and their submissions are handed to the draw recording thread as ordered tasks instead of draining it first (~15 waits a frame). gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:376, gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.h:234 BB_PIPE_SPIN_US integer µs ≥0 (200 with 12+ CPU threads, else 50) How long the draw-pipe consumer spins waiting for work before sleeping. Lower values leave more CPU to the game on few-core machines (Steam Deck). gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_draw_pipe.h:209 BB_PREP_WORKERS integer 0–16 (half the CPU threads, clamped 1–8) Number of idle-priority worker threads that prepare draws speculatively ahead of the GPU thread (pipeline and resource selection). 0 = none. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_draw_prep.cpp:54 BB_PREUPLOAD 0 = off, 1 = rewritten memory already in VRAM only (no new VRAM), 2 = all of the game's GPU memory (~3 GB more VRAM); without run.sh unset = 0 Launcher: Advanced > Performance > "Background pre-upload into VRAM" (run.sh exports 1 when unset). Background upload of the game's GPU memory into VRAM ahead of use: fewer hitches when areas load. Always off with BB_GUEST_IN_PLACE (the GPU reads the game's memory itself). gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:386, run.sh:197, launcher/bbport_launcher.py:661 BB_PREUPLOAD_MB integer MiB per frame (16) Most memory the background pre-upload (BB_PREUPLOAD) puts into VRAM per frame. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:1625 BB_READBACKS 0 = off, 1 = relaxed, 2 = precise (1 = relaxed) Launcher: Advanced > Performance > "GPU data readbacks by the CPU" (Relaxed = unset, Off = 0, Precise = 2). shadPS4's GPU readback mode. Relaxed by default: without readbacks FaceGen reads stale GPU-written vertices (vertex explosions). 2 also read-protects GPU-written pages and disables BB_GPU_WRITE_TWINS. gpu/shim/core/emulator_settings.h:27-29, launcher/bbport_launcher.py:659, 524-525 BB_READBACK_LINEAR 1/y/t or 0 (off) shadPS4's readback of linear (untiled or narrow) images to guest memory. gpu/shim/core/emulator_settings.h:66, gpu/shadps4/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.cpp:786 BB_READBACK_QUEUE 0 = off; unset/other = on Uses a separate compute/transfer queue to read back GPU data finished long ago, without waiting behind the queued frame. 0 turns it off. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_instance.cpp:499 BB_STAGING_KEEP_MB integer MiB (512) How much of the staging upload ring is kept (and populated at startup) instead of being trimmed when idle; re-creating blocks during streaming bursts caused stutter. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_staging_buffer_pool.cpp:27 BB_SUBMIT_AHEAD integer >= 0 (2) The first K submissions of a frame do not wait for the previous frame, so translation overlaps the GPU (1080p Yahar'gul: 101 -> 154 FPS). 8 or more leaked the game's heap; if the heap grows anyway K becomes 0 for the session. gpu/shadps4/core/libraries/gnmdriver/gnmdriver.cpp:134-149 BB_TEXTURE_HELPER 1 = on, 0 = off (unset = off) A spinning helper thread binds textures for the draw recording thread. Measured neutral on 16 threads, so opt-in. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.cpp:2195 BB_UFFD first char 1 = on (run.sh: 0) Internal (run.sh exports 0 when unset). Write tracking with userfaultfd write-protection instead of mprotect (no address-space write lock); falls back to mprotect if the kernel lacks it. Off by default: the Steam Deck crashed with it. Ignored with BB_GUEST_GPU_MEMORY=1. run.sh:272, gpu/shadps4/video_core/page_manager.cpp:545-551, 723-737 BB_VBLANK_HZ Hz; 0 or >120 = uncapped (60 if unset in the library) Internal (run.sh derives it from BB_FPS (uncap 480, 90 90, else 60). Vblank rate. Above 120 Hz (or 0) a finished frame is presented at once instead of on the next vblank tick; 60/90 are the fixed-timestep presets. gpu/shim/core/emulator_settings.h:30, run.sh:280 BB_VK_RECORD_THREAD 0 = off; unset/other = on Vulkan commands are recorded on dedicated recording threads. 0 records on the calling thread (suspected in vertex explosions, issue #39). gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_scheduler.cpp:120 BB_VK_RECORD_THREADS integer 1–8 (3 with 12+ CPU threads, 2 with 8+, else 1) Number of Vulkan recording threads; the command stream is cut into segments recorded in parallel. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_scheduler.cpp:97 BB_VK_SEGMENT_KB integer KiB ≥1 (64) Size of command-stream segments handed to the recording threads (~60 draws per 64 KiB). gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_scheduler.cpp:127 BB_VMA_BLOCK_MB integer MiB ≥1 (64; VMA's own default is 256) Size of Vulkan memory allocator blocks. Smaller blocks are returned to the driver sooner when freed. gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_instance.cpp:906 BB_VMA_DEDICATED_MB MiB; 0 = never (4) Images of this size or more get dedicated memory, returned to the driver when freed (shared VMA blocks left ~0.9 GB of holes after texture evictions). gpu/shadps4/video_core/texture_cache/image.cpp:107-113 BB_VRAM_IDLE_SECONDS seconds (60) Mirrored (VRAM-copied) blocks not bound for this long go back in place. gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:1823, gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h:412 BB_VRAM_PRESSURE_IDLE_SECONDS seconds (3) Near the critical VRAM mark, blocks no binding used directly for this long (an area left behind) go back in place first, longest unused first. gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache_layer.cpp:903-913 BB_VRAM_PRESSURE_PERCENT percent, max 95; 0 = off (85) How full VRAM is against the driver's budget: "tight" from this percent, "full" 5 points above (fewer VRAM copies then). gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:2045 BB_VRAM_PROMOTE_PERCENT percent (90) Past this share of the driver's VRAM budget no new VRAM copies are made; candidates wait and are read in place meanwhile (issue #32: 8 GB cards). gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.cpp:3944 MESA_SHADER_CACHE_MAX_SIZE size (run.sh default 4G) Mesa's shader cache size, larger than Mesa's default. run.sh:31 __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE run.sh default 1 NVIDIA's shader disk cache on (run.sh default; keeps compiled pipelines between sessions). run.sh:25-30 __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_SIZE bytes (run.sh default 10737418240) NVIDIA's shader cache size (10 GiB by default here). run.sh:30 __GL_SHADER_DISK_CACHE_SKIP_CLEANUP run.sh default 1 NVIDIA's shader cache without its size cleanup (as Steam sets it). run.sh:29

Not when SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER is set. run.sh BB_STEAM_OVERLAY 1 = on (default 0) Launcher: Setup → Game → "Steam overlay", under "Add to Steam" (saved as soon as it changes). docs.title: Layer memory module: PS4 GPU addresses without sparse (plan, 2026-10-09)
Why
docs.text: The new memory model keeps game memory in a single sparse arena and moves blocks between game memory and VRAM by rebinding (vkQueueBindSparse). On NVIDIA (Linux, drivers ≥ 555), the bind time grows with the number of pages already bound, and the call holds a global lock: each move to VRAM cost seconds, and the game and the desktop froze (GTX 1660 Ti, 615.71). Without moves (BB_FIXED_ARENA=1) it runs at 48.6 FPS versus ~205 on an RX 7800 XT. We need a model that works the same on AMD, NVIDIA and Intel and is not tied to the shadPS4 buffer cache: part of a future layer for running PS4 games.

docs.title: Idea
docs.text:
The PS4 GPU has its own virtual memory (GPUVM) on top of shared memory; every V#, T# and pointer in user data is a virtual address. On PC we do the same with Vulkan 1.2 means (BDA):

  • Memory sources: ordinary (non-sparse) Vulkan buffers:
  • chunks of game memory: dma-buf (AMD) or host memory import (NVIDIA, Intel), one chunk per game direct memory allocation (allocations are mapped whole, so a range inside one mapping is always contiguous within one chunk);
  • VRAM mirrors: segments aligned to game addresses (game page X sits in the segment at the same offset), allocated when the first VRAM page appears in the segment.
  • Page table (a buffer on the GPU): page of a PS4 address → device address (BDA) of its current source. It is changed by a copy in the command stream, in order with draws, without semaphores.
  • Direct path: the whole V# range is in one source (almost all bindings) → an ordinary descriptor (source buffer, offset, size). The shader translator does not change.
  • Paged path: the range is mixed (≈85 huge bindings per frame: shaders bound to all of memory) → the descriptor points to a record {PS4 address, size}, and the shader translates each address through the table. A pipeline variant only for such bindings (specialization key).
  • Vertices, indices, indirect arguments, copies, texture uploads: the direct path; otherwise, assembly into a contiguous temporary buffer (read-only) or per-page copies (the CPU knows the table).
  • Moving to VRAM and back: the policy of the current new model (data whose writes we know about: loaders, the GPU; unknown writers stay in place), but the execution is a copy + a table write + choosing the source at bind time. Bindings recorded before a move read the old source, which is still valid; VRAM is freed once the GPU has passed those commands.

docs.title: Order of work
docs.text:
1. Module core (gpu/layer/, no dependencies on shadPS4): sources, pages, table, Resolve(address, size) → a direct source or "mixed", walking over sources for copies. The command recording interface is abstract (copy, table write), so it does not pull in the scheduler.
  2. Hook-up without VRAM: the new model returns ranges in place through chunk buffers, not through the arena; the new model does not create the sparse arena. Expected: ~48 FPS on AMD (like BB_FIXED_ARENA), no vkQueueBindSparse at all. Check the image, then make a build for NVIDIA.
  3. VRAM mirrors + moves: the policy from BufferCache, the page table, the paged path in shaders for mixed bindings. Goal: parity with the sparse arena on AMD (~205 FPS).
  4. NVIDIA/Intel: a test build, a tester log; then remove sparse from the new model entirely.

Measurements: RX 7800 XT, standing still (tools/bench.sh), BB_PC_MODEL=1; diagnostics BB_RESIDENCY_MIX=1.

docs.title: Status (2026-10-09, morning)
docs.text:
• Steps 1–3 are done. On the RX 7800 XT, standing still: module ~205 FPS, sparse arena ~205–238, old model ~220 (at the lamp in the Hunter's Nightmare); in another spot (1170 draw calls): 167.5 / 164.5 / 146. vkQueueBindSparse is never called in module mode (counter in the Layer memory: line).
  • Mixed bindings are solved without the paged path: "volatile" blocks (layer_volatile). A block with unknown bytes (the edge of a range, a gap between images) goes into the mirror together with the rest of the range, is refreshed from game memory before each binding, and whatever a dispatch wrote into it is copied back after the dispatch (LayerAfterBindings). The paged path remains for bindings of 64 MiB and larger. BB_LAYER_VOLATILE=0 turns it off (for comparison).
  • Default: AMD uses the sparse arena, other GPUs use the module (BB_LAYER_MEMORY=1/0 to choose manually). Step 4 (NVIDIA): needs a tester log; the host memory import path cannot be checked on AMD (RADV does not import memfd).

docs.title: Addendum: original copying and portable labels (2026-10-09)
docs.text: In the new module, the paged path of the original copy shader is fixed: writes update game memory and the current mirror; the native shader is now selected by default. For GPU labels, a standard Vulkan path without AMD buffer marker was added. The implementation, switches and verification limits are described in TRANSLATION_GPU_COPY_LABELS.ru.md. This removes the dependency of label writes on the AMD extension, but does not replace hardware testing on NVIDIA.

docs.title: Mods and third-party patches
docs.text: Both are in the launcher's Mods section and apply at the next start. The game folder itself is never changed.

docs.title: File mods
docs.text:
The Mods group has the folder, a Load mods switch, and the list of mods: each one can be turned on or off and moved up or down. The lowest mod that is on wins: when two mods replace the same file, the log says which one replaced the other.

The mods folder is ~/.local/share/bbport/mods/ with the AppImage (mods/ in the data directory when running from the repository). Extract each mod into a folder of its own:

mods/
  Mod name/
    dvdroot_ps4/
      chr/...
      param/...
      menu/...

These layouts work as well:

  • Mod name/app0/dvdroot_ps4/..., and Mod name/<title ID>/dvdroot_ps4/... with whichever release the mod was made for (CUSA03173, CUSA00900, ...).
  • Up to three extra wrapper folders, as extracting an archive into a folder of its name leaves it: Mod name/Mod name v1.2/dvdroot_ps4/... (notes, pictures and links may sit next to them: README, .txt, .pdf, .png, .webp, .url, ...).
  • The game's folders without dvdroot_ps4: Mod name/chr/..., Mod name/parts/... (chr, parts, map, menu, msg, param, sfx, sound, font and the other folders of dvdroot_ps4), also next to other folders such as Screenshots or Optional, which stay out of the game.

A folder in the mods folder that is not a mod is listed in the launcher under the mods with the reason: still an archive, several mods in one folder, no game files, or empty.

Upper or lower case does not matter: a mod made on Windows with DVDROOT_PS4/Chr/C0000.chrbnd.dcx replaces the game's dvdroot_ps4/chr/c0000.chrbnd.dcx. The log shows how many game files the mods replaced and added, e.g. Mods: 12 game files replaced, 0 added. A mod meant to replace files that says 0 game files replaced has its files in the wrong place.

What works: ready-made replacements of dvdroot_ps4 files (textures, models, params, interface, sound, fonts). What does not:

  • ZIP or 7z archives: extract them first.
  • Two mods changing different parts of the same .dcx or .bnd file: the last one replaces it whole, the files are not merged.
  • Mods that replace eboot.bin, sce_module or sce_sys, DLL injectors and script plugins. Changes to the game's code are patches (below).
  • Symbolic links inside a mod.

Whether a mod works with Bloodborne 1.09 is up to its author.

A shadPS4-style folder next to the game folder, <game folder>-mods/dvdroot_ps4/... (for example CUSA03173-mods next to CUSA03173), is loaded too, before the mods in the list. You can also choose a folder that holds dvdroot_ps4 directly as the mods folder: it is then loaded as one mod. Load mods turns all of them off. The launcher's button prompts and gestures menu work the same way, as files laid under the mods; they are settings of their own and stay on when mods are off.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
For each start, the data directory gets a merged tree of links, out/mod-game-*: the game sees the mods' files where they replace its own and the original files everywhere else. /app0 is read-only, and saves go to the usual folder. The tree is removed when the game exits normally or the launcher stops it; one left behind by a crash is not reused.

The order and the mods turned off are kept in mods.json in the data directory:

{"order": ["First", "Second"], "disabled": ["First"]}

New folders are turned on and added at the end, in alphabetical order.

From a terminal:

BB_GAME_DIR=/path/to/game BB_MODS_DIR=/path/to/mods bash run.sh
BB_GAME_DIR=/path/to/game BB_MODS_ENABLED=0 bash run.sh

BB_MODS_CONFIG sets another mods.json. BB_MOD_TRACE=1 (with BB_MODS_DIR) logs the first reads of files that come from mods, to see whether a mod is being used.

docs.title: Third-party patches
docs.text:
The Third-party patches group loads patches in the shadPS4/GoldHEN XML format from the patches folder: ~/.local/share/bbport/patches/ with the AppImage, or another folder chosen in the launcher.

  • Only patches for version 01.09 of eboot.bin are listed. Files for other games are skipped: a file applies when it lists any retail release of Bloodborne, or none.
  • Each patch starts on or off as the file says (isEnabled); the choice in the launcher is kept in patches.json in the data directory:
{"enabled": ["file.xml/Patch name"], "disabled": ["file.xml/Other patch"]}
  • Lines of type bytes, bytes16, bytes32, bytes64, float32, float64, utf8 and utf16 work. A patch with a mask line (a pattern search) or an address outside the executable is skipped whole, and the log says so.
  • They apply after bbport's own patches (patches/Bloodborne.xml), so where both change the same bytes, the third-party patch wins.
  • shadPS4's patch file can stay named Bloodborne.xml. In a file of that name, the patches named as one of bbport's own are left out (bbport's apply), and the rest start off until you turn them on, whatever the file says. An older package's copy of bbport's file adds nothing.
  • Patches that replace pointers in tables, such as 60 FPS++, are moved to where the game is loaded.

From a terminal: BB_PATCHES_DIR=/path BB_PATCHES_CONFIG=/path/patches.json bash run.sh.

This guide is based on bbport's MODS.md (Russian), by deadinside28.

docs.title: Online play and co-op
docs.text:
Online play is a beta. Messages, bloodstains and ghosts come from a community game server: Seamless Hunt's (the default) or The Hunter's Dream. Bells and summons go through a co-op pool, and then the players' games connect to each other. Linux and Windows players can play together: everyone needs the game at version 1.09 and the same pool.

shadPS4's public shadNet server no longer accepts bbport builds: it signs the game out right after the login ("This shadNet server doesn't accept your shadPS4 build" in the log), and the launcher says so. The pools for bbport are Seamless Hunt (the default), The Hunter's Dream's and a server of your own.

docs.title: Seamless Hunt
docs.text:
Seamless Hunt is a community server for Seamless Co-op (BBSC), where Windows players join with BBSC's package for the Windows port.

  1. In the launcher's Multiplayer → Online tab, turn on Play online and choose Seamless Hunt: its shadNet server, WebAPI and game server come with it.
  2. Type a name and a password under Account and press Create (once). The server wants an email for each account; the launcher makes one from the name, as Seamless Hunt's own tool does.
  3. Turn on BBSC in the Seamless co-op (BBSC) group and press Test in the Status row.

Its bloodstains and death visions crash the game with "Transaction failed", on Windows too: they are off by default, as in Seamless Hunt's package (Bloodstains on Seamless Hunt brings them back). Messages, ghosts and summon signs are not affected.

docs.title: The Hunter's Dream (with bbhost's players)
docs.text:
Choose The Hunter's Dream (with bbhost players) in the launcher's Multiplayer → Online tab. bbbridge by MaskZeus starts with the game, stands in for a shadNet server on this computer and talks to The Hunter's Dream the way bbhost does, its relay included, so no router port is needed. The account is The Hunter's Dream's, kept in user/bbbridge (no password):

  • Sign in with Discord: the launcher shows a code and opens The Hunter's Dream's page; approve it there. The account is the same one bbhost uses.
  • Without Discord: type a name and Create. Keep the recovery code the launcher shows: with the name, it brings the account back on another computer (Recover).

The game's play log (its own telemetry) stays blocked, so The Hunter's Dream's live map does not show you.

This connection is unofficial. The Hunter's Dream's team has not approved bbbridge, and they do not support bbport: report problems here (issues), not to The Hunter's Dream's support.

docs.title: Your own server
docs.text:
Its owner creates the account (hosting your own server), or you make it with Create under Account when the server lets anyone register.

  1. In the launcher's Multiplayer → Online tab, turn on Play online, choose Your own server with its address, and enter the account name (not the email) and the password. The password is kept on this computer with the launcher's settings.
  2. Press Test in the Status row: the game server, the shadNet server, its UDP port and its WebAPI should all answer, and with the account filled in, the sign-in should work. A wrong name or password shows there (the server does not say which of the two).

If the game says you are not signed in to PlayStation Network, the shadNet login failed: the log then has a shadNet login error (code 8 is a wrong name or password). If the server did not answer when the game started, the game keeps trying in the background.

docs.title: Seamless co-op (BBSC)
docs.text:
BBSC (Bloodborne Seamless Co-op, by CLS_AMG) keeps a co-op session going through deaths, lamps, areas, bosses and the Hunter's Dream, for up to 5 hunters: the guest follows the host through lamps, sees the host's world (doors, bosses, lifts), keeps the items and echoes it gets, and enemies get stronger for every guest. It runs inside the game (bbsc/, loaded as libbbsc.so). It is new, and its own author marks much of it as untested.

  1. In the launcher's Multiplayer → Online tab, turn on BBSC in the Seamless co-op (BBSC) group. BBSC settings has its options (the same as in BBSC's Windows launcher); the defaults are BBSC's.
  2. Every player of the session needs BBSC, the same version: on Linux this port, on Windows BBSC's package for the Windows port (its BBport release). A player without it plays the normal game.
  3. The server decides how much of it works:
  4. BBSC's game server (Seamless Hunt's, which comes with it, or your group's, hosted with it): everything, summons across areas and 5 hunters included. Set it as the Game server of the Online tab.
  5. The Hunter's Dream: the session stays together (deaths, lamps, bosses), but summons are the normal game's: BBSC turns its own summon changes and the 5 hunters off on public servers. Its messages go straight between the players.

With BBSC and BBSC's game server, two players who cannot reach each other directly (CGNAT, strict routers, two games on one PC) are connected through that server's UDP relay (port 3478); SHADPS4_P2P_RELAY=0 turns it off. Without BBSC, and on The Hunter's Dream (bbbridge relays by itself), the relay is off.

BBSC gives every character its own items, which cost no Insight: the Hunt Bell (call other players), the Kin Bell (join another player), the Bloodlust Bell (invade), the Duel Bell (PvP on and off during co-op) and the Parting Blank (end co-op). It takes the game's Beckoning Bell, Small Resonant Bell and Silencing Blank out of the inventory, and they do not come back when BBSC is turned off; BBSC's own items stay, with their names (scripts/bbsc_kit_texts.py), and work again when it is back on. Before changing anything it backs the saves up to user/bbsc/save-backups/: copy a character's save from there to play it without BBSC with its old bells. Its texts follow the game's language (Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese and Russian; English otherwise). F8 puts you back on the ground if you get stuck inside another player.

Not yet tested with more than one player on Linux: one player alone works (its items, deaths, lamps, the Hunter's Dream). Report what you find with the log.

Its log is in user/bbsc/logs/ (in the AppImage, ~/.local/share/bbport/user/bbsc/logs/), and the game's log has its warnings (BBSC: lines). Not in the Linux build: BBSC's cinematic camera (L3 + R3 opens bbport's menu) and its own Discord status (bbport has one).

docs.title: Summoning in the game
docs.text:
• The host rings the Beckoning Bell (one Insight each time); the helper rings the Small Resonant Bell. With BBSC: the Hunt Bell and the Kin Bell, at no Insight cost.
  • Use the same password in the game's network settings, so you find each other whatever your levels.
  • Be in the same area, close to each other, with the area's boss still alive in the host's world.

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
Co-op traffic is UDP, straight between the players' computers. With your own server on Tailscale (hosting your own server) it goes through Tailscale: turn UPnP off and skip this section. Otherwise each player has to be reachable from the Internet:

  1. The router. With UPnP on (the default), the game opens its port on the router itself: the log says UPNP: mapped UDP port <port>. A router without UPnP needs a port forward by hand (UDP, the pinned port below, to your computer's LAN address).
  2. Pin the port when you open it by hand or in a firewall: Co-op port (UDP) in the Online tab, for example 3658 (0, the default, is a random port each time). The log then says P2P transport ready: UDP physical_port=3658.
  3. Open it in the firewall. UPnP opens the port on the router only, not in this computer's firewall. With ufw or firewalld on, the launcher's Multiplayer → Online tab says so and gives the commands. For ufw: 
    sudo ufw allow 3658/udp
sudo ufw allow from <router IP> proto udp    # the router's UPnP answers
    Windows players open the same UDP port in their own firewall.

A router whose public address is shared by many customers (CG-NAT) cannot forward ports: the log's UPNP: IGD found - external IP=... should be your real public address. Tailscale works behind CG-NAT too.

docs.title: Reading the log
docs.text:
Run with BB_GPU_LOG=info in the extra variables for the online details. In a summon:

Line Meaning Logged in npid='...' The shadNet login worked. summon_messenger/create Your sign is placed (helper). summon_messenger/get, sceNpMatching2CreateJoinRoom, summon_messenger/request The host found the sign, made the room and sent the summon. peer '...' endpoint unresolved shadNet has no address for the other player: its UDP port did not answer. Online: the shadNet server ... does not accept this build The server refuses bbport (shadPS4's public one): use Seamless Hunt, The Hunter's Dream or your own server. event=0(DEAD) The connection gave up.

docs.title: Hosting your own co-op server
docs.text:
Bells and summons go through a shadNet server. shadPS4's public one (srv.shadps4.net) no longer accepts bbport builds, and the public pools for bbport are Seamless Hunt (the default) and The Hunter's Dream's, through bbbridge (the launcher's Multiplayer → Online tab; README). A group of friends can also run their own server: shadnet-p2p by Wozzardman, the shadNet server with that UDP port working and a summon service of its own.

With your own shadNet server, messages, bloodstains and ghosts come from the Game server field of the Online tab: The Hunter's Dream by default, or BBSC's game server (below). Windows players of Supermedo's port can join the same server.

Tested with two players, one on this Linux port and one on Supermedo's Windows port, over Tailscale, with the server below on a home server (Ubuntu 26.04): summons, a boss fight together and summoning again after the helper died.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
• One always-on computer runs the server: a VPS, a home server, or one of the players' PCs (then it has to be on while you play).
  • Everyone joins one Tailscale network (a tailnet): the server and every player. Tailscale gives each computer an address starting with 100. and encrypts the traffic between them. This matters: shadNet's login on TCP 31313 is not encrypted, so it should not be open to the Internet. And the games then reach each other over Tailscale too, so nobody has to open ports on their router.
Protocol Port Used for TCP 31313 Login and matchmaking UDP 31314 Each player's address, for the other player of a summon TCP 31315 WebAPI and the summon service

docs.title: 1. Tailscale
docs.text:
On the server and on every player's computer, install Tailscale (download; on Linux curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh) and sign in:

sudo tailscale up

The server's owner invites the players from the admin console (Users → Invite external users), and each player accepts the invitation and signs in on the computer they play on. Then, on the server:

tailscale ip -4    # the server's address, 100.x.y.z: the players need it
tailscale status   # every player's computer should be listed

docs.title: With Docker (any Linux)
docs.text:
This repository has a Docker image for it: tools/shadnet-server. It builds shadnet-p2p on Debian 13, because shadnet-p2p needs Qt 6.8 or newer and some distributions are older (Ubuntu 24.04 has Qt 6.4). It runs on any Linux with Docker, Ubuntu 24.04 included.

mkdir shadnet-server && cd shadnet-server
for f in Dockerfile entrypoint.sh; do
    curl -fsSLO "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ayozetr/bloodborne_linux/main/tools/shadnet-server/$f"
done
docker build -t bbport-shadnet .

Then start it, with the server's Tailscale address and a signup code of your own (letters, digits, - and _; the players never need it, only you, to create their accounts):

docker run -d --name shadnet --restart unless-stopped --network host \
    -v shadnet-data:/data \
    -e SHADNET_HOST=100.x.y.z \
    -e SHADNET_REGISTRATION_KEY=a-long-code-of-your-own \
    bbport-shadnet
docker logs shadnet

The log should end with the three listeners on the Tailscale address:

Unsecured TCP listener on: 100.x.y.z:31313. No encryption, use it only on trusted networks
STUN UDP listener on: 100.x.y.z:31314
WebApiServer listening on: 100.x.y.z:31315

SHADNET_HOST keeps the server off the computer's other networks. After a reboot, it waits until Tailscale is up. The configuration (shadnet.cfg) and the accounts (db/shadnet.db) live in the shadnet-data volume. To stop or update the server:

docker stop shadnet && docker rm shadnet    # the volume, with the accounts, stays
docker build -t bbport-shadnet .            # after downloading a newer Dockerfile

Then run the same docker run again.

docs.title: Without Docker
docs.text: Follow shadnet-p2p's README. It needs Qt 6.8 or newer: Arch Linux and its derivatives, Debian 13, Ubuntu 26.04, Fedora 41 or newer. On Debian and Ubuntu, install qt6-websockets-dev along with the packages it lists, or CMake does not find Qt's HTTP server module (checked on Debian 13 and Ubuntu 26.04). In build/shadnet.cfg, set Host to the server's Tailscale address (or 0.0.0.0), Matching2Enabled=true and RegistrationSecretKey to your signup code.

docs.title: A firewall on the server
docs.text:
With ufw, let the tailnet in:

sudo ufw allow in on tailscale0

docs.title: 3. Accounts
docs.text:
One account per player, created on the server with the signup code. The name is 3 to 16 letters, digits, - or _:

docker exec shadnet shadnet-sample 127.0.0.1 31313 register <name> <password> <email> <signup code>

127.0.0.1 works only when the server listens on every address (SHADNET_HOST unset or 0.0.0.0). With SHADNET_HOST set, use that address instead. The tool answers Account created successfully., or FAILED: Unauthorized when the code is wrong. Give each player their own name and password.

To back up the accounts, stop the server and copy the volume's db/shadnet.db.

docs.title: 4. Each player's launcher
docs.text:
In Multiplayer → Online:

Setting Value Play online On shadNet server Your own server Server address 100.x.y.z (the port, 31313, is added) WebAPI address Empty (the server's port 31315) Online ID / Password The player's own account UPnP Off (Tailscale needs no router ports)

Then press Test in the Status row. Every line should get a check mark, the shadNet server's UDP among them: it shows the address the server sees for you, a 100. one through Tailscale. An error mark on the UDP line means summons cannot connect: check that the server is running and that its log lists the UDP listener.

Summons go through the server's own summon service: the log of a game says Co-op: summon signs through http://100.x.y.z:31315.

Windows players set the same server, WebAPI and account in the Windows port's launcher.

docs.title: Seamless co-op (BBSC)
docs.text:
For BBSC with everything on (summons across areas, 5 hunters), the group also runs BBSC's game server next to shadNet. It is in this repository, bbsc/server/gameserver/bbsc_gameserver.py (Python 3, nothing to install), and it takes the place of The Hunter's Dream for messages, bloodstains and the server list.

  1. Turn on shadNet's seamless mode: run the shadNet container again with -e SHADNET_BLOODBORNE_SEAMLESS_COOP=1 (it is kept in its shadnet.cfg).
  2. Build and start the game server on the same computer, with the same Tailscale address:
mkdir bbsc-server && cd bbsc-server
for f in Dockerfile entrypoint.sh; do
    curl -fsSLO "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ayozetr/bloodborne_linux/main/tools/bbsc-server/$f"
done
docker build -t bbport-bbsc-server .
docker run -d --name bbsc-server --restart unless-stopped --network host \
    -v bbsc-data:/data -e BBSC_HOST=100.x.y.z bbport-bbsc-server
docker logs bbsc-server

BBSC_SHADNET is the shadNet server's address when it is on another computer. Messages, bloodstains and its logs live in the bbsc-data volume. Without Docker: python3 bbsc/server/gameserver/bbsc_gameserver.py --shadnet 100.x.y.z --host 100.x.y.z.

Port Protocol What 20443 TCP The game server (messages, bloodstains, ghosts) 20444 TCP BBSC's relay (warps, world sync, scaling) 18671 TCP Its bbhost-compatible service (BBSC_BBHOST=0, --no-bbhost, turns it off) 3478 UDP The relay BBSC players fall back to when they cannot reach each other directly

Each player then sets Game server to http://100.x.y.z:20443 in the launcher's Multiplayer → Online tab, keeps the same shadNet server and account, and turns on BBSC in the Seamless co-op (BBSC) group. BBSC finds its relay at the game server's address (or BBSC_RELAY, the relay address in BBSC's settings).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The log shows 127.0.0.1 or another address in the listeners: check SHADNET_HOST, or Host in the shadnet.cfg beside the server's executable.
  • Waiting for 100.x.y.z in the log: Tailscale is not up on the server, or the address is wrong (tailscale ip -4).
  • The game says it is not signed in to PlayStation Network: a wrong name or password (code 8 in the log), or two players using one account.
  • The test passes but summons fail: every player's computer must be in the tailnet, not only the server; tailscale ping <player> from each side. Everyone needs the game at version 1.09 and the same co-op mode.

See also Online play and co-op for the bells, passwords and log lines of a summon.

docs.title: Our own translator instead of shadPS4: structure and order of work (2026-10-10)
docs.text: Goal: move away from emulation and from shadPS4 code. We want our own PS4 command translator and our own graphics renderer that scale to other games (everything specific to one game lives in its profile, gpu/games/) and behave the same on AMD and NVIDIA. After that comes shadnet (online play).

docs.title: Current state
docs.text:
Borrowed from shadPS4 (gpu/VENDOR.txt, commit b4e7ae7 from 2026-09-24): about 116k lines.

Part Lines What it does Our work in it video_core/amdgpu 8.3k PM4 parsing (command processor liverpool.cpp), registers, tiling GPU-side labels, occlusion, predication, PM4 self-test video_core/renderer_vulkan 28.6k Vulkan renderer: pipelines, rasterizer, scheduler, presenter draw pipeline (stages A/B), recording threads, upscalers, background compilation video_core/buffer_cache 7.4k game memory for the GPU almost all rewritten (memory module, VRAM copies, traps) video_core/texture_cache 4.8k textures by address, detiling time-based collector, uploads shader_recompiler 38.6k GCN → IR → SPIR-V paged buffers (BDA), fixes core, common 21.8k VideoOut, GnmDriver, event queues, utilities vblank, labels

Our own code, outside shadPS4: gpu/layer/ (memory module BbLayer::GpuMemory), gpu/games/ (game profiles), gpu/shim/ (overlay, settings, hooks), the runtime in src/ (kernel, libc, files, saves).

docs.title: Target structure
docs.text:
Modules with narrow interfaces. None of them knows addresses in the game's code (that belongs to the profile), and none does the GPU's work on the CPU (that is emulation):

  1. memory: game memory in place, VRAM copies as a cache, shared tracking of page protection (write traps for copies and textures). Exists: layer/ + the module in buffer_cache_layer.cpp.
  2. cp: command processor. Parses PM4 into the translator's command stream (state, draws, dispatches, synchronization) in the order the GPU executes it. Replaces liverpool.cpp.
  3. state: context registers → pipeline keys and Vulkan dynamic state. Replaces liverpool_to_vk and the key building in vk_pipeline_cache.
  4. resources: V#/T#/S# descriptors → buffers, images, samplers (caches, detiling). Replaces buffer_cache, texture_cache (the buffer part is already almost ours).
  5. render: Vulkan. Command recording per thread, barriers, submission, presentation. Replaces renderer_vulkan (the scheduler and stages A/B are already ours).
  6. shaders: GCN → SPIR-V. The largest part; it is replaced last, stage by stage (decoder, IR, passes, code generation).
  7. platform: VideoOut, GnmDriver, kernel events (core/libraries), next to the runtime.
  8. games: game profiles (exists).

docs.title: Order
docs.text:
One module is replaced at a time. First an interface in our code with the shadPS4 code behind it as is, then our own implementation behind the same interface. After each step: the route (a route benchmark script (not in this repository), frames and snapshots), the PM4 self-test (BB_PM4_SELFTEST=1), unit tests, the game on AMD and (from tester logs) on NVIDIA.

Step What Why in this order 1 memory: shared tracking of page protection; write traps under textures by default; model 0.3 and the sparse arena are removed removes the rest of memory emulation and the dependency on game hooks 2 cp: the translator's command stream; MEM_SEMAPHORE, GPU time, compute queues done by the GPU the last emulation left is in the command processor 3 state + resources they build on 1 and 2; the buffer part is already ours 4 render the scheduler and stages are already ours; the rasterizer and pipelines remain 5 shaders the largest and riskiest; by then everything else is already ours 6 shadnet networking, once the graphics are our own

Steps 1 and 2 are the plan to move away from emulation (EMULATION_REMOVAL_PLAN.ru.md, section dated 2026-10-10).

docs.title: 2026-10-10: our own PM4 decoder (step 2, start)
docs.text:
• gpu/cp/: our own code, without shadPS4. Packet format and opcodes (cp_pm4.h), register file and decoder (cp_decoder.{h,cpp}). The decoder walks the buffer in stream order, applies register packets (SET_*_REG, CLEAR_STATE, registers written by draw packets), descends into nested buffers and hands each packet to a "sink" (BbCp::Sink) with the state already applied: draws and dispatches as typed calls, the rest as packets. The sink decides COND_EXEC. The decoder knows nothing about Vulkan, the game or where execution happens.
  • Unit test tests/test_cp_decoder.cpp (target cp-decoder-test): registers, partial writes, draws, dispatches, nested buffers, COND_EXEC, CLEAR_STATE, corrupt buffers.
  • Register addresses are checked against the shadPS4 layout at build time (static_assert). This found a bug: on CIK, CP_STRMOUT_CNTL is in uconfig (0xC03F), not in config.
  • Shadow check in the game (BB_CP_SHADOW=1): the new decoder parses every top-level buffer from the same state, and the register files are compared at the end of the buffer. On the route, all buffers matched (~800k buffers, ~200 million packets, 0 mismatches, 0 parse errors). Bloodborne does not use nested buffers (they are covered by the unit test).
  • Next: the decoder as a cursor (packet by packet, so the command processor loop can yield to other queues while waiting), the register file as shared state storage (its layout matches shadPS4 Regs word for word), then moving packet handling from liverpool.cpp into the translator's sink one packet type at a time, each time with the shadow check and the route.

docs.title: 2026-10-10: the new decoder is the real parsing path
docs.text:
• The decoder became a cursor (BbCp::Cursor: packet by packet, nested buffers at the caller's choice). The register file can live in the owner's storage (for the command processor, its regs, with the same word layout). A write observer (RegisterObserver, one call per packet) provides what draw preparation needs: the written blocks and the packet checksum.
  • ProcessGraphics takes packets and register writes from the cursor (BB_CP_DECODER=0 selects the old walk). What each packet does is still the old code. PM4 self-test: 11 of 11. The share of prepared draws is the same (747k used, 19k not, versus 755k/24k), so the checksums match. The image is the same.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: When asking for help, attach the log: in the launcher's Log section, Export log… saves it to a file and Copy puts it on the clipboard.

docs.title: The launcher rejects the game
docs.text:
The launcher checks the game folder before starting. What it says, and what to do:

Message What to do bbport needs the 1.09 update merged into the game folder Copy everything from the dumped 1.09 update into the game folder, replacing files (eboot.bin and sce_sys too). param.sfo is from 1.09 but eboot.bin is not Copy eboot.bin from the dumped 1.09 update over the old one. This eboot.bin has the 60 fps patch by Lance McDonald applied Use a clean eboot.bin from the 1.09 update. bbport has its own 60 FPS. This is not a retail release of Bloodborne Alpha tests and other games do not run. See supported releases. eboot.bin could not be read as a decrypted PS4 executable Dump the game and the update again. The game files are damaged The extraction tool broke compressed files (LibOrbisPkg PkgTool on .NET 6 or newer); the game would hang while loading. Extract the game and the update again with a fixed tool.

docs.title: The game shows New Game instead of my save
docs.text:
Saves live in the data directory, and each way of running the port has its own:

  • The AppImage: ~/.local/share/bbport/user/savedata/1/<title ID>/.
  • From the repository (run.sh): user/savedata/1/<title ID>/ in the repository.

To move a save, close the game, back up both folders, and copy the savedata folder over.

docs.title: DLSS is "not supported by this GPU"
docs.text:
The log says why, on a line starting with DLSS:.

  • DLSS needs a GeForce RTX (20 series or newer) and NVIDIA's own driver; it does not work with NVK.
  • The 0.4-linux.1 AppImage ships a modified copy of NVIDIA's DLSS library, which the driver refuses (Feature requirement query failed: 0xbad00012): update to 0.5-linux.1 or newer.
  • From the repository, DLSS needs bash tools/build_dlss.sh once after build.sh.
  • If the log says Device creation with DLSS extensions failed, NVIDIA's CUDA/UVM module is missing: the game then uses FSR 3.1. Load it with sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm (the nvidia-modprobe package loads it when needed); with Secure Boot, a module signing key that is not enrolled stops it (Key was rejected by service).

docs.title: Spanish shows the Latin American text (or the other way round)
docs.text: The game picks a language's regional text by the dump's region. Choose it in Setup → Game region: Europe for Spanish from Spain, The Americas for Latin American Spanish.

docs.title: The game crashes after playing a while, on a card with little VRAM
docs.text: On a 6 GB card the texture cache can run out of video memory: the log then repeats Texture cache: memory pressure, ... (critical ...). Lower what uses VRAM: a 60 FPS limit, a lower output resolution, lower Model detail in the game's Display settings, and close other programs that use the GPU (browsers, video players, other games).

docs.title: The picture is stretched on an ultrawide screen
docs.text: Graphics → Display → Output resolution lists 2560×1080, 3440×1440, 3840×1600 and 5120×2160 (21:9) and 3840×1080 and 5120×1440 (32:9); any other size written as output_res=WxH in bbport.ini works too. The view gets wider instead of stretched: the game's camera, its HUD and the lock-on and health-bar markers are patched at start for the screen's own aspect ratio. HUD position moves health, items and Blood Echoes from the centred 16:9 area (as on a 16:9 screen) to the screen edges, and menu backdrops cover the whole width. These sizes need the startup patch: changing them in the game restarts it, and TAA (which needs live resolution changes) leaves them stretched. aspect_patch=0 in bbport.ini turns the wider view off.

docs.title: Quit to Desktop is missing from the menus, or shows another name
docs.text:
Mods → Menus and debugging → Quit to Desktop in the title and System menus (also in the in-game menu; on by default) adds the entry to the title menu and to the System menu. The title entry closes the game at once; the System entry runs the game's own Exit Game first (it saves, and its confirmation asks to quit to the desktop), and the game closes when it is back at the intro or the title screen. The log then says Runtime: Quit to Desktop, and the game ends with exit code 0, as when the window is closed.
